NEW DELHI: India’s record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism, but the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. After returning from Glasgow with a historic haul of seven gold and three silver medals, India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.The CWG triumph underlined the country’s growing depth, particularly in women’s boxing. Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg), Jaismine Lamboria (57kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg) and Arundhati Choudhary (70kg) struck gold, while Sachin Siwach (60kg) and Ankush Panghal (80kg) topped the podium in the men’s competition. Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain, Jadumani Singh and Narender Berwal added silver medals.The challenge in Aichi-Nagoya, however, will be on an entirely different scale. Unlike the Commonwealth Games, the Asian Games will feature continental powerhouses such as Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, China, Chinese Taipei, Japan and North Korea — nations that have consistently dominated the World Championships and the Olympics.Uzbek stars Mirazizbek Mirzakhalilov and Bobo-Usmon Baturov, along with Kazakhstan’s Kairat Yeraliyev and Ablaikhan Zhussupov, are expected to headline a field packed with world-class talent.India will also be without two of its Commonwealth champions. Jaismine (57kg) and Arundhati (70kg) will miss out because their weight categories do not feature in the Asian Games programme, depriving the country of two genuine medal prospects.“The Asian Games for us is like the Olympics,” Boxing Federation of India president Ajay Singh said. “The best teams in the world today are Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and India, and all three are in Asia. Add a strong Chinese contingent and you understand why it is much tougher. You can’t replicate this (CWG) performance at the Asian Games. But if you win a sizeable number of medals at the Asian Games, you can be hopeful of winning medals at the Olympics too.Women’s head coach Santiago Nieva shared a similar assessment while insisting the team remains on the right path.“We can’t guarantee that we will win gold all the time, but we are on the right track. We know how strong the field will be at the Asian Games. The boxers are aware that they can’t sit on their success,” he said.India had returned with one silver and three bronze medals from the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. The Glasgow CWG showcased the strides the boxing contingent has made. But it’ll be Aichi-Nagoya that is going to reveal whether the progress is enough to challenge Asia’s finest and signal genuine medal potential for the 2028 Olympics.
Article Summary: India's record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism. But the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.

Pakistani boxer Qudratullah has reportedly gone missing in Glasgow, just hours before the country’s Commonwealth Games contingent was scheduled to leave for home.According to a report by Pakistani outlet Geo News, sources in the Pakistan Boxing Federation said Qudratullah was last seen in his hotel room at around 2am. Article Title: ‘Like preparing for IIT and UPSC together’: Father Murali shares Sreeshankar’s comeback story
Article Text:
Murali Sreeshankar

KOCHI: S Murali gave an unusual analogy to describe the struggles his son, long jumper Sreeshankar Murali, undertook to regain full fitness after a career-threatening knee injury he sustained two years ago.“Sreeshankar’s comeback was as difficult as preparing for the IIT and Civil Services simultaneously,” he told TOI.Murali is currently near Prague, where he is closely monitoring his son’s training ahead of a busy stretch that begins with the World Athletics Continental Tour (silver level) meet in Bhubaneswar on Aug 22, followed by next month’s Asian Games in Japan.“Sreeshankar’s training now revolves around strength and conditioning, along with the prehab and rehab programme designed by coach Wayne Lombard. There is very little time to work on technique. The priority is to protect the knee on his take-off leg,” Murali said.His IIT-UPSC analogy aptly captures the magnitude of the challenge Sreeshankar faced after suffering the devastating injury just months before the 2024 Paris Olympics.Two years later, the journey came full circle when the 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.“Of all the medals Sreeshankar has won, this one gives me the greatest satisfaction because of the circumstances under which he achieved it. It reflects his mental toughness and hunger,” Murali said.The conditions in Glasgow were anything but favourable.“It was around 12 degrees Celsius with drizzle and strong winds, making the runway tricky,” Murali said. Despite the difficult conditions, Sreeshankar produced a best jump of 8.09m to finish second.The performance inevitably brought back painful memories of 2024, when the family received a grim diagnosis after Sreeshankar tore the patellar tendon in his take-off leg.“The doctors in Mumbai had not seen an injury like this. I thought he would never be able to walk again,” Murali recalled.“They told us it wasn’t a common sports injury but the kind usually seen after a serious car accident. His knee was completely ruptured.”Determined to find the best treatment, Murali travelled nearly 1,900 miles with his son to Doha’s Aspetar Hospital. “The surgeons reconstructed his knee using four screws.”The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process.The painstaking recovery paid rich dividends. Since returning to elite competition, Sreeshankar has consistently cleared the eight-metre mark, including a season’s best of 8.38m at the Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar in June.“There is no time to bask in the Commonwealth Games glory,” Murali said, pointing to the demanding schedule ahead.Sreeshankar will now turn his attention to the Asian Games in Japan, where he hopes to upgrade the silver medal he won at the previous edition in Hangzhou.“With everything Sreeshankar has gone through, he has every reason to believe he can stand on top of the podium at the Asian Games,” Murali concluded.
Article Summary: Sreeshankar Murali suffered a career-threatening knee injury two years ago. The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process. The 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week's Commonwealth Games.

Article Title: Report: Lionel Messi could get one final Argentina appearance as captain in front of home fans despite retirement
Article Text:
Argentina's Lionel Messi celebrates at the end of the World Cup quarterfinal soccer match against the Netherlands in Lusail, Qatar, Dec. 10, 2022. (AP Photo/Ricardo Mazalan, File)

Argentina could organise Messi farewell match

Messi's World Cup farewell may not have been his last

Argentina's Lionel Messi (10) reacts after the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi, left, and defender Maximiliano Falcon (37) celebrate after midfielder Casemiro (5) scored the side's first goal during the first half of an MLS soccer match against CF Montreal, Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026, in Miami. (AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)

Argentina still have to decide who replaces Messi as captain

Lionel Messi may have already played his final competitive match for Argentina, but reports suggest his farewell to the national team could still have one more chapter. Messi confirmed his retirement from international football in a lengthy post on social media, with the 2026 World Cup final against Spain expected to mark the end of his Argentina career. Yet Argentina could organise a special farewell match for their captain during the next FIFA international window. Nothing has been confirmed, and the Argentine Football Association would first need to establish whether Messi himself wants to take part, but the possibility is already being discussed. If it happens, it could give Argentina's supporters the chance to say goodbye to their greatest player on home soil.According to reports from Argentina, the AFA is considering arranging a farewell appearance for Messi during the next FIFA international window, which runs from September 21 to October 6.The federation is expected to organise two or three friendly matches, with some reports suggesting Argentina could play as many as three or four during the window. The opponents, dates and venues have not yet been confirmed.Argentine journalist Pablo Gravellone of Todo Noticias reported that all signs point towards Messi playing his final Argentina match at home.A potential venue is Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, where Argentina regularly plays its home matches. There is also a possibility of the national team taking the occasion to Rosario, Messi's hometown, although that is considered less likely.TNT Sports Argentina's Maximiliano Grillo reported: "Argentina are working to arrange two or three friendly matches in September. The games are expected to be played in Buenos Aires, Cordoba and/or Rosario, with the opponents yet to be confirmed."That leaves plenty still to be decided.There is currently no confirmed opponent, match date or venue for a Messi farewell, and the idea remains at the reporting stage rather than an official AFA announcement.Most importantly, Argentina would first need to speak to Messi and determine whether he is willing to return for the occasion.The possibility of another appearance comes only days after Messi announced his international retirement.On August 31, the Inter Miami star confirmed that he had decided to end his Argentina career after a remarkable 207-cap international career, during which he scored 125 goals and won six major titles, most notably the 2022 World Cup.His decision followed Argentina's 2026 World Cup final defeat to Spain, which appeared to bring his international career to a close.A farewell match would therefore be very different from another competitive fixture. Argentina would not be trying to give Messi one more tournament run; instead, the occasion would allow the player and supporters to formally close a chapter that ended in very different circumstances in the World Cup final.It would also allow Messi to say goodbye in front of Argentine supporters rather than ending his international career thousands of miles from home.Messi remains an active professional footballer at club level with Inter Miami, with his contract extending beyond this international retirement. That means there is no immediate issue surrounding his fitness or ability to play another match should he agree to the idea.The proposed farewell would also not necessarily resemble a traditional retirement exhibition, where former teammates and friends gather for a ceremonial game. The reports point instead towards Messi appearing for Argentina in an official international friendly, potentially wearing the captain's armband one final time.For now, though, that remains dependent on discussions that have yet to take place.While the possibility of one final Messi appearance is being discussed, Argentina also have to begin preparing for life without the captain who has led them through one of the most successful periods in their history.Cristian Romero appears to be one of the leading candidates to inherit the armband. The defender has already captained Argentina on several occasions when Messi was unavailable and is regarded as a natural leader within the squad.He is not the only possibility.Emiliano "Dibu" Martinez and Enzo Fernández have also been mentioned as potential successors because of their experience, importance to the team and standing within the dressing room.There is another complication, however.Nicolas Otamendi, who had generally taken the captain's armband whenever Messi was not in the starting XI, had already announced his retirement from international football immediately after the World Cup.That means Argentina enter their next era without the usual succession option that had existed behind Messi.A farewell match could therefore provide an unusual moment for the transition. Messi could potentially lead Argentina one last time before the armband officially passes to a new generation.But until the AFA confirms its plans, even that remains uncertain.And there is one more question waiting for the next generation: who wears the No.10 after Messi?Reports have suggested Nico Paz could be the preferred choice, but only if Lionel Scaloni renews his contract as Argentina head coach. That decision is expected to be discussed in the coming months, meaning even Messi's eventual successor remains tied to what happens with Scaloni.
Article Summary: Argentina could organise Messi farewell match during next FIFA international window. Reports suggest Argentina could play as many as three or four friendly matches. The opponents, dates and venues have not yet been confirmed. Argentina would first need to speak to Messi and determine whether he is willing to return for the occasion.

Article Title: Argentina can't retire Messi's legendary No.10 because of the same FIFA rule that stopped them honouring Maradona in 2002
Article Text:
Argentina cannot retire Messi’s iconic No.10 because FIFA requires every World Cup squad number from 1 to 26 to be assigned/ Image: file

Argentina wanted to retire Maradona’s No.10 too

A pedestrian carries a bucket past graffiti depicting late soccer legend Diego Maradona in Buenos Aires, Argentina, Monday, April 13, 2026. (AP Photo/Rodrigo Abd)

Why FIFA will not let Argentina retire the shirt

Argentinian super fan Miloslav Urbanec shows his statue of Diego Maradona on a day of the World Cup semifinal match between Argentina and England, in the village of Bukovka, Czech Republic, Wednesday, July 15, 2026. (AP Photo/Petr David Josek)

Must read:

Messi’s No.10 has become impossible to separate from his legacy

Sport

Must read:

The next No.10 will inherit a shirt unlike any other

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lionel Messi’s retirement from international football has left Argentina with a question that feels almost impossible to answer: what happens to the No.10 shirt now? For many supporters, the obvious answer is to retire it forever. Messi wore it for two decades, became Argentina’s most-capped player and all-time leading scorer, and turned the shirt into one of the most recognisable symbols in world football. But Argentina has tried to do this before, when Diego Maradona was the player being honoured, and FIFA stopped it. More than two decades later, the same regulation stands in the way of giving Messi the ultimate tribute.The idea of retiring Argentina’s No.10 is not new, and its strongest precedent comes from the country’s other footballing icon.On 25 September 2001, the Argentine Football Association voted unanimously, on the initiative of then-president Julio Grondona, to retire the No.10 shirt in honour of Maradona.The plan was to put the decision into effect before the 2002 World Cup, and at the time it appeared to be settled. Argentine newspaper Olé even ran a front-page headline declaring: "It is God's will."There was, however, one problem: FIFA had its own rules governing squad numbers at its tournaments.FIFA rejected Argentina’s request, meaning the No.10 could not simply disappear from the World Cup squad. Ariel "El Burrito" Ortega ultimately wore the shirt for Argentina at the 2002 tournament, becoming the player who wore the famous number most prominently between the Maradona and Messi eras.The significance of that episode has returned now that Messi has stepped away from the national team.This time, it is not Maradona’s name attached to the request. It is Messi’s.The obstacle is not a lack of willingness from Argentina. It is the numbering system FIFA applies to its official tournaments.According to Marca, FIFA regulations require tournament squad lists for competitions such as the World Cup and Copa America to use consecutive numbers from 1 to 26. Every player selected for the 26-man squad must therefore have a number, with none omitted.That makes retiring the No.10 impossible in an official tournament.Argentina could want to leave the number untouched, supporters could overwhelmingly back the idea and the Argentine Football Association could decide that nobody should wear it again, but the regulations would still require the No.10 to be assigned to somebody when the team enters a tournament governed by FIFA's squad-number rules.In other words, Argentina cannot simply submit a 26-man squad numbered 1 through 9 and 11 through 27, or leave the No.10 blank as a permanent tribute to Messi. The numbering requirement creates a direct conflict with the idea of permanently retiring the shirt.That is exactly what happened with Maradona.The regulation therefore means Messi's No.10 can be treated differently in friendly matches, where Argentina could choose not to use the number, but the situation changes as soon as the national team enters an official tournament.The desire to retire the shirt is understandable because Messi did far more than simply inherit Maradona's number.He wore No.10 for Argentina for roughly two decades and leaves the national team as its all-time leading scorer and most-capped player. His international career also transformed the meaning of the shirt for another generation of Argentine supporters, just as Maradona had done before him.That is why the debate is not really about who deserves to wear the number next. It is about whether anybody should wear it at all.The Argentine Football Association has previously expressed a clear desire to retire the shirt once Messi ended his international career.In 2024, AFA president Claudio Tapia told: "The national team's number 10 shirt will be retired when Messi ends his international career."Tapia's comments made the association's intention clear, but the practical problem was always going to be FIFA's tournament regulations.The situation leaves Argentina with an unusual compromise. The No.10 could effectively be reserved as Messi's number whenever the team plays certain friendlies, allowing the association and supporters to honour him without giving the shirt to another player.But when the next World Cup or Copa America arrives, the number cannot simply be erased from Argentina's squad list.Someone will have to wear it.That leaves Argentina facing another difficult question: if the No.10 cannot be retired, who takes it?Messi's successor will inevitably inherit a shirt carrying the weight of both him and Maradona. It is one thing to wear the No.10 for Argentina; it is another to wear the number that has belonged to two of the country's greatest footballers.Several names could enter the conversation, including Alexis Mac Allister, Enzo Fernández, Thiago Almada and Nico Paz.According to ESPN Argentina insider Federico Bueno, Argentina have an internal plan for Paz to take the No.10 if Lionel Scaloni renews his contract as head coach, with negotiations expected to take place in the coming months.For now, though, the immediate reality is simpler: Messi's No.10 cannot be permanently removed from Argentina's official tournament squad.Maradona's Argentina tried it in 2001 and FIFA said no. More than 20 years later, the same rule means Messi's shirt faces the same fate.
Article Summary: Lionel Messi’s retirement from international football has left Argentina with a question that feels almost impossible to answer. For many supporters, the obvious answer is to retire it forever. Argentina has tried to do this before, when Diego Maradona was the player being honoured, and FIFA stopped it. FIFA regulations require tournament squad lists for competitions such as the World Cup and Copa America to use consecutive numbers from 1 to 26.

Article Title: Messi’s iconic No.10 successor revealed as 21-year-old star set to inherit legendary shirt if one condition is met
Article Text:
Nico Paz could inherit Argentina’s iconic No.10 shirt after Messi, but one condition must first be met/ Image: Instagram

Nico Paz reportedly chosen to inherit Messi's No.10

Why Paz has emerged as the choice

Messi leaves behind an enormous legacy

Argentina's Lionel Messi (10) cries at the end of the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

A huge shirt for Argentina's next generation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lionel Messi's retirement from international football has left Argentina with one of the most difficult shirts in world football to fill. The No.10 has belonged to Messi for years after previously carrying the legacy of Diego Maradona, and the player reportedly chosen to inherit it is one of Argentina's brightest young talents. Nico Paz has emerged as the reported successor to the iconic shirt, but there is one important condition attached to the plan.According to ESPN Argentina, Argentina have already identified Paz as the player they want to hand Messi's No.10 shirt to, although the decision is tied to Scaloni's future with the national team.The 21-year-old attacking midfielder has previously worn No.18 during his 11 appearances for Argentina, but he could now take on the number associated with two of the country's greatest-ever footballers.ESPN Argentina insider Federico Bueno reported that the plan has already been decided internally and is being taken seriously."If Scaloni renews as Argentina's coach, which is expected to be negotiated in the coming months, the No. 10 shirt will go to Nico Paz. This has already been decided internally and is being taken very seriously," Bueno said.That means Paz's succession of Messi is not yet unconditional. Scaloni's contract situation must first be resolved, with the 48-year-old expected to negotiate a new deal in the coming months.Scaloni has been Argentina's head coach since 2018 and oversaw the side's run to the 2022 World Cup title in Qatar before taking them to the 2026 World Cup final. If he agrees to continue in the role, Paz is reportedly set to become the next No.10.There are more established names within the Argentina squad who could have been considered for such an iconic shirt, including Enzo Fernandez and Alexis Mac Allister, but the reported succession plan points towards Paz as the player viewed as capable of leading the next generation.Paz, 21, was born in Spain but is the son of former Argentina international Pablo Paz. He came through the Real Madrid academy and made eight first-team appearances for the Spanish giants before leaving for Italian club Como in 2024.His development in Serie A has accelerated under former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas, with Paz establishing himself as one of the most exciting young attacking players in European football.He has made 77 appearances in all competitions for Como, scoring 19 goals, while his performances have repeatedly fuelled speculation that Real Madrid could bring him back to the Bernabeu.A return to Madrid has reportedly been tipped in virtually every transfer window since his departure, underlining how highly the Spanish club continues to regard the player it developed.For Argentina, however, his development has taken on a different significance.Paz has already earned 11 senior caps and is now being considered for a role that carries considerably more weight than simply becoming another attacking option in the squad.Whoever takes the No.10 will inevitably be compared with Messi, even if Argentina's next generation has no realistic way of reproducing what the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner achieved.Messi departs the national team as a former world champion, having captained Argentina to glory in Qatar in 2022, and as the country's long-standing No.10 and leader.He leaves after 207 international appearances, having built a legacy that also places him as the second-highest goalscorer in World Cup history.His decision came after Argentina's defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final in New Jersey, with Messi making clear that he felt his international journey had reached its natural conclusion."It was a decision that hurt – and still hurts deep down – but I understand that the time has come," Messi said in his retirement statement."I swear to you that I always gave it my all – not just in these last few years when we won everything, but before that too; I always fought and left everything on the field for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football.""Time is running short, chapters come to a close, and this is one that hurts me deeply. I love, have loved, and will always love being part of the national team.""I’ve given everything I had; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are some great young players coming up who deserve to be here."The significance of the No.10 means Paz would not simply be inheriting a squad number.Argentina's shirt has already carried the weight of Diego Maradona, who famously wore it during his World Cup-winning campaign in 1986, before Messi created his own extraordinary chapter in the number.That makes the decision to give it to a 21-year-old a significant statement about how Argentina view Paz's potential.The Como playmaker is still at an early stage of his international career, with only 11 appearances to his name, and he has never been expected to simply replace Messi as a player. Instead, the reported decision reflects the belief that he can become one of the central figures in Argentina's post-Messi era.There is still one hurdle before that succession can happen.Scaloni's future must first be settled. If the World Cup-winning coach agrees a new contract, the reported plan is for Paz to move from the No.18 he has worn during his early international career into Messi's iconic No.10.For now, that remains a reported internal decision rather than an officially confirmed shirt change. But if Scaloni stays, Paz appears set to become the young Argentine entrusted with carrying the most famous number in the country's football history into its next era.

Article Title: 20-year-old Real Betis star breaks down in tears alongside mum after being forced to leave boyhood club to fund veteran's return
Article Text:
After 15 years at Betis, Pablo Garcia was forced out on deadline day despite recently becoming a first-team regular/ Image: Instagram, X

Garcia leaves Betis after 15 years

A tearful farewell on deadline day

Betis chose Ceballos amid salary-limit pressure

Betis fans question the decision

Pablo Garcia's 15-year journey with Real Betis came to an emotional end on deadline day, with the 20-year-old breaking down in tears as he said goodbye to the club he joined as a six-year-old. Garcia had become a first-team regular and had played in all three of Betis' league matches this season, including scoring a late winner against Valencia last week, but strict LaLiga salary limits left the club needing to make a difficult financial decision. Betis ultimately sanctioned his move to Racing Santander to create room for the return of former academy star Dani Ceballos.Garcia joined Betis at the age of six, arriving at the club at pre-Benjamin level before working his way through the academy and eventually breaking into the senior side.His progress had turned him into a regular first-team player, making his departure particularly difficult for everyone involved. The 20-year-old had featured in all three of Betis' league games this season before the deadline-day move and had recently provided a memorable moment by scoring a late winner against Valencia.He leaves having made 33 first-team appearances for the club, scoring three goals.His next destination is Racing Santander, with the Spanish second-tier club agreeing a deal that sees them acquire 50 per cent of Garcia's federative rights for €5 million.Betis have also retained a percentage of any future sale and secured a right of first refusal on the young Spain Under-21 international, ensuring the club has a degree of protection should his career continue to develop away from Seville.But while the transfer represents a significant deal for a young player, the circumstances surrounding it were far more painful for Garcia.Garcia was visibly emotional as he left Betis' stadium late on Tuesday evening, wiping away tears as he waved goodbye to supporters.He was later seen in a car alongside his mother, still visibly upset after saying farewell to the club that had been part of his life for 15 years.The youngster made no secret of the fact that leaving was not what he wanted."It is a very difficult time for everyone, but we have to keep our heads up and look forward. I hope to return, that is what we all want," Garcia told Spanish media."There were many things I could not influence. I wish everything had gone as we had all hoped. Thank you very much from the bottom of my heart to all Betis fans."His father also spoke about the family's pain during an interview with Radio COPE."This is really hard for us. If that is how Betis fans feel, imagine how we must feel. It was 15 years, a whole eternity," he said.Garcia's farewell came after an extremely late and complicated deadline-day operation, with Betis needing to complete the move quickly to create the financial space required for another piece of business.The player at the centre of that decision was Dani Ceballos, another product of the Betis academy who was returning to the club after years away.Ceballos, now 30, came through Betis' youth system before establishing himself with the senior side and leaving for Real Madrid in 2017. He spent nine years under contract with Madrid in total, including two seasons on loan at Arsenal, before making his return to his boyhood club.Betis agreed a three-year contract with Ceballos that will keep him at the club until 2029.The problem was LaLiga's strict financial regulations and the salary limits governing what clubs can spend. Betis needed to free up sufficient room to register Ceballos, leaving the club with a choice between retaining Garcia and creating the financial space required for the veteran midfielder's return.Garcia's sale was therefore accelerated late on deadline day, with his departure providing the necessary financial manoeuvring. The move was also described as Betis' sole permanent departure generating full profit since July 1.For Garcia, however, the financial calculation offered little comfort. He had spent almost his entire life at Betis and had only just established himself as a first-team regular.The decision understandably provoked a strong reaction among supporters.News of Garcia's departure left sections of the Betis fanbase stunned, particularly given how recently he had become an important member of the senior squad.Some supporters directed their anger towards the club, while others blamed LaLiga president Javier Tebas and the financial restrictions that had left Betis needing to make such a choice.One fan wrote on X: "Shameless! You don't do this to family!"Another posted: "Aren't you ashamed?"A third supporter wrote: "This really is sad. We have to blame [Javier] Tebas [president of LaLiga]."The possibility of a future return is now part of his new chapter at Racing Santander, particularly because Betis have retained a percentage of his future rights and a right of first refusal.There was also a touching final message from Garcia as he left the club, when he told reporters: "Let's hope everything goes well, I wish you all the best in the Champions League."For a player who joined Betis as a six-year-old and spent 15 years progressing through the club, it was an emotional way to close one chapter, even if the door has not been completely shut behind him.Meanwhile, Ceballos could make his second Betis debut against former club Real Madrid this weekend, while Betis' next league fixture is against Rayo Vallecano on Saturday. The two sides are scheduled to meet again in December.
Article Summary: Pablo Garcia left Real Betis on deadline day after 15 years at the club. The 20-year-old had become a first-team regular for the LaLiga club. But strict salary limits left the club with a difficult financial decision. They decided to sell Garcia to Racing Santander to make room for Dani Ceballos. The decision provoked a strong reaction among Betis fans.

Article Title: Real Madrid star Raul Asencio in trouble again! Banned from driving for 8 months days before trial over alleged sharing of explicit video involving minor
Article Text:
Real Madrid defender Raul Asencio receives eight-month driving ban and $16,685 fine after drink-driving conviction in Spain/ Image: X

Asencio stopped at 6.30am in Gran Canaria

A difficult period for the Real Madrid defender

What happened in the separate video case?

Real Madrid's patience with Asencio is being tested

Real Madrid defender Raul Asencio has been handed an eight-month driving ban and a fine of around £12,350 (approx. $16,685) after being convicted of drink-driving in Spain. The 23-year-old was stopped in the early hours while driving a Porsche Macan GTS in Gran Canaria and recorded a breathalyser reading almost four times above the country's legal limit. The conviction comes just days before Asencio is due in court over a separate case involving the alleged sharing and distribution of intimate footage involving a minor, for which he has previously denied the allegations. Real Madrid have also opened disciplinary proceedings against their academy graduate following the latest incident.Asencio was stopped by police at a breathalyser checkpoint in San Bartolome de Tirajana, in the south of Gran Canaria, at around 6.30am on August 16.The Real Madrid defender had been driving a Porsche Macan GTS when officers stopped him and carried out a breath test. According to the Daily Mail, his reading came back at 0.90 milligrams of alcohol per litre of exhaled breath, while Spain's legal drink-drive limit is 0.25 milligrams per litre.He subsequently pleaded guilty to drink-driving at a fast-track hearing three days later.The conviction, which emerged on Wednesday, resulted in an eight-month suspension of his driving licence and a financial penalty of €14,400, equivalent to around $16,685.The fine was set at €120 (approx. $139) per day over four months.The incident has now also triggered action from Real Madrid. According to journalist Melchor Ruiz, the club has opened an extraordinary disciplinary file against Asencio, meaning his conduct will now be assessed internally as well as having already resulted in a criminal conviction.Under the collective agreement between La Liga and the AFE (Association of Spanish Footballers), the incident could potentially be treated as either a serious or very serious disciplinary offence.If Real Madrid classifies it as a serious offence, Asencio could face a suspension from his salary lasting between two and 10 days. A very serious classification would carry a substantially heavier punishment, with a salary suspension of between 11 and 30 days, while a fine could reach 25 per cent of the first €100,000 of his monthly salaryThe timing of the drink-driving conviction is particularly significant because Asencio is already dealing with a separate legal case that is due to reach trial on Thursday.The Real Madrid defender is facing proceedings over the alleged sharing and distribution of an intimate video involving a minor, as well as allegations that the footage was distributed without consent.Both alleged victims have since withdrawn their complaints against Asencio, which has opened the possibility of him being acquitted.However, public prosecutors are still seeking a two-and-a-half-year prison sentence if he is convicted. Prosecutors have also indicated that they will withdraw the charges against Asencio if the alleged victims confirm in court the apologies they say he offered them during the judicial investigation.Asencio has previously denied the allegations. In May 2025, he released a statement in which he fiercely rejected the accusations made against him.The separate case dates back to an incident at a beach club in Gran Canaria on June 15, 2023.Asencio's former Real Madrid academy teammates Ferran Ruiz, Juan Rodriguez and Andres Garcia are also due to stand trial in connection with the 2023 incident.Ruiz, Rodriguez and Garcia were arrested in September 2023 after allegations surrounding sexual activity involving two women at the beach club. The three former Real Madrid academy players are accused of having consensual sexual relations with the two women but allegedly recording and distributing sexual videos without their consent.Asencio is not accused of being involved in that alleged incident itself.He was initially interviewed by police in connection with the investigation before subsequently becoming part of the wider case over the alleged sharing of the footage.The legal issues come during a period in which Asencio's position at Real Madrid has already become considerably less secure than it once appeared.The defender was previously viewed as one of the leading products of the club's academy after breaking into the first team, but his standing has declined in recent months. He is currently out injured and, according to the report, has fallen down the pecking order to the point where he is not even considered the club's fourth-choice central defender.His relationship with the club has also reportedly been complicated by his decision to remain at Real Madrid during the summer transfer window, despite the club's preference for him to leave. That decision was reported to have prevented the hierarchy from pursuing further defensive reinforcements.The drink-driving conviction now adds another issue for the club to consider, with Real Madrid's extraordinary disciplinary proceedings potentially bringing an internal punishment on top of the legal consequences already imposed by the Spanish court.
Article Summary: Raul Asencio given eight-month driving ban and $16,685 fine after drink-driving conviction in Spain. 23-year-old was stopped in the early hours while driving a Porsche Macan GTS in Gran Canaria and recorded a breathalyser reading almost four times above the country's legal limit. Real Madrid have also opened disciplinary proceedings against their academy graduate.
